# Tomato Sauce

## Ingredients

- 3 kg ripe tomatoes, ideally san marzano
- 2 onions, finely chopped
- 6 garlic cloves
- 100 ml olive oil
- 1 large bunch basil
- 2 tsp salt
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp citric acid per jar
- 500 ml jars, sterilised

## Method

Blanch the tomatoes in boiling water for a minute, then slip the skins off and chop them. Cook the onions in olive oil until soft, add the garlic, then the tomatoes and the salt. Simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and a spoon leaves a trail. Bruise the basil and drop it in for the last ten minutes. Blend it smooth or leave it rustic, both are good.

The tomatoes should taste sweet and deep before they go in a jar. I add 1 tsp citric acid per jar to keep the tomatoes safely acidic, plus the sugar to round them out. Fill hot 500 ml jars to a centimetre from the rim, wipe the threads, and cap.

## Jars and Keeping

Process the jars in a 40-minute water bath, counting from when it returns to a full boil. Lift them out and let them cool undisturbed for 12 hours, then check the seals by pressing the centre of each lid.

A jar that sealed keeps a year on the shelf. Once opened, it goes in the fridge and gets used within a week. With san marzano and a good bunch of basil this beats anything from a shop, and I make a batch every September while the tomatoes are at their best. I label each jar with the date and the variety, which pays off when I open one in February. A little sauce goes a long way on pasta, and the rest of the jar stretches through a braise.
